Available steps for a step selection check on simulated tracks

available_steps.Rd

For each moving step of tracks simulated with a habitat_selection() model, returns the step the animal took and n control steps drawn from the same movement kernel: from the step's start and heading, one step length and one turn from the model's samplers, any goal pull, and reflection at the shore. A conditional logit of case on the layer, with one stratum per step, then estimates the step-scale selection coefficient, which for a log-linear preference is the beta the tracks were simulated with: clogit(case ~ depth_m + strata(stratum), data = steps), with the survival package attached.

Usage

available_steps(tracks, layer = NULL, n = 10, seed = NULL)

Arguments

tracks

A sim_tracks object from simulate_tracks() with a model from habitat_selection(), as returned, with its attributes. Use beta = 0 for a walk with no preference.

layer

NULL to read the selection's own layer, or a terra::SpatRaster with the geometry of the tracks' grid, one column per layer, named by the layer names.

n

Number of control steps per step.

seed

Seed for the control steps; NULL uses the current random number stream. The caller's stream is restored after a seeded call.

Value

A data frame, n + 1 rows per moving step: path_id, step (the step that ends at the used position, as in tracks), stratum (one per path and step, for strata()), case (1 for the step taken, 0 for a control), x, y and cell of the end of the step, one column per layer with its value at the cell, and step_length, the straight-line distance in metres from the start of the step to its end. Attributes n

and epsg.

Details

The estimator is consistent here because the controls come from the kernel that proposed each step, so the ratio of used to available is the preference alone. Steps of a resting animal, of an animal at its goal and steps held after 1,000 rejected candidates have no heading and are left out.

Matching each used step with control steps drawn from a distribution of steps, then fitting a conditional logistic regression, is step selection analysis as Avgar et al. (2016) describe it. Their integrated form also estimates the movement kernel from the data. Here the kernel is the simulation's own and is known exactly.

References

Avgar, T., Potts, J. R., Lewis, M. A. and Boyce, M. S. (2016). Integrated step selection analysis: bridging the gap between resource selection and animal movement. Methods in Ecology and Evolution, 7, 619-630. doi:10.1111/2041-210X.12528 (Step selection analysis, p. 620: each used step matched with available steps drawn from a distribution of steps.)

See also

habitat_selection(), simulate_tracks()

Examples

lake <- terra::rast(system.file("extdata", "stoney_depth.tif",
                                package = "arraydesign"))
depth <- abs(lake)
names(depth) <- "depth_m"
shallow <- habitat_selection(crw_model(30, 15, 40), depth, beta = -0.3)

# Three animals for 6 hours, fewer than a check needs, to keep the
# example short
tracks <- simulate_tracks(lake, shallow, n_animals = 3, n_steps = 360,
                          seed = 1)
steps <- available_steps(tracks, n = 10, seed = 2)
head(steps)
#>   path_id step stratum case        x       y cell depth_m step_length
#> 1       1    1       1    1 734907.2 4939597 4011       0    47.13950
#> 2       1    1       1    0 734942.4 4939582 4011       0    15.17355
#> 3       1    1       1    0 734945.1 4939580 4011       0    14.48830
#> 4       1    1       1    0 734947.0 4939581 4011       0    12.78524
#> 5       1    1       1    0 734932.6 4939573 4011       0    28.04219
#> 6       1    1       1    0 734942.0 4939579 4011       0    17.23459

# A conditional logit on the three animals, to set against beta = -0.3
# (clogit() reads a bare strata() term, so survival is attached)
if (requireNamespace("survival", quietly = TRUE)) {
  library(survival)
  fit <- clogit(case ~ depth_m + strata(stratum), data = steps)
  coef(fit)
}
#>    depth_m 
#> -0.1959405 
# Three animals are too few for the estimate to sit near -0.3; section 5 of
# vignette("movement-models") fits 20 animals over 48 hours, and the 95%
# interval of their mean holds -0.3.
